source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-3: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 3 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat this as a provisional cluster_troubleshooting analysis for RoCE variant 3. Assume a multi-node GPU collective workload, but do not assume that RoCE is lossless, that GPU-direct is active, or that the observed path is the intended one. First inventory node/GPU/NIC and switch-port topology, affinity, PCIe/NVLink paths, route symmetry, firmware/driver/library versions, MTU, link speed, VLAN/priority mapping, queue-pair count, message-size and concurrency distributions, clocks, and any transport fallback; label measured facts, estimates, and unknowns separately. Trace the application and collective library through verbs work requests/completions, registered host or GPU buffers, queue pairs, NICs, switch fabric, and peer, and distinguish application communication/step timing from device counters.

Hypothesis and test: with placement, workload, warm-up, sample count, and software held constant, an interleaved matched baseline will show that the suspected RoCE path or identified configuration change reduces p95 and p99 collective latency by at least 10% without increasing p99 step time, timeout/retry rate, drops, pause duration, ECN marks, queue depth, link errors, CPU/GPU utilization, or correctness failures. Test the hypothesis by checking MTU consistency, route symmetry, PFC priority and pause behavior, ECN marking/thresholds, buffer occupancy, congestion, retransmissions, queue-pair completions, NIC and switch error counters, and whether a fallback transport is masking the fault. Use synchronized timestamps, distributions rather than averages, explicit units, repeated randomized/interleaved trials, and confidence intervals; correlate counters to the affected operations instead of treating any single counter as causal.

Mitigation must be staged and reversible: change one documented setting at a time on a canary, verify collective outputs and application progress, and retain a host-staging or alternate-transport control. Roll back on a predeclared p99 regression, timeout/retry storm, persistent pause/drop/error growth, link instability, or any data-integrity/correctness failure. Do not prescribe vendor-specific PFC/ECN values or claim causality without configuration, topology, synchronized telemetry, representative workload, matched-baseline, and fallback evidence. Protect telemetry by minimizing identifiers and access; require operator approval for disruptive fault injection.
risks: RoCE losslessness, PFC/ECN behavior, topology, GPU-direct path, and fallback are platform-dependent and unverified.
Device or switch counters may not explain end-to-end tail latency without timestamp correlation.
A mitigation can increase pauses, retries, drops, or correctness risk if applied without a canary.
evidence_required: topology, route, MTU, priority, PFC/ECN, firmware, and transport/fallback inventory
interleaved matched baseline with workload and sample distributions
synchronized application, verbs, NIC, switch, queue, pause, ECN, error, and link telemetry
correctness checks and explicit rollback thresholds from a canary
